text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities — A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 — ran in about 49–52 in 100 cases in the earlier window and in about 98–100 in 100 cases in the later window, in the later window essentially once per case (mean occurrences per trace ≈ 1.0). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- In the earlier window these six formed two mutually exclusive groups: {A33, A35, A36} ran in about 49 in 100 cases and {A37, A38, A39} in about 51 in 100, with both groups in the same case in at most about 1–2 in 100 cases; within a group the activities always ran together, in no fixed order (A33 before A36 in about 23 in 100, A36 before A33 in about 25 in 100). [REL037, REL038, REL044, REL055, REL056, REL059, REL039, REL041, REL045, REL050, REL052]
- In the later window both groups ran in the same case in about 98 in 100 cases, with a fixed order between the groups — A33/A35/A36 before A37/A38/A39 in about 95–98 in 100 cases — while the order within each group stayed mixed (A33 before A36 about 46 in 100, A36 before A33 about 50 in 100). [REL039, REL040, REL041, REL045, REL046, REL047, REL050, REL051, REL052, REL037, REL038, REL055, REL056, REL059]
- The groups sit between activities that ran in every case in both windows: A14 and A30 now precede the first group in about 95–98 in 100 cases (earlier in about 47–52 in 100, the share of cases in which the respective group ran), and both groups now precede A31, A47 and A48 in about 95–99 in 100 cases (earlier about 47–52). Direct successions shifted accordingly: A33, A35 and A36 now lead to A37/A38/A39 instead of A31, and A30 leads to A35/A33/A36 instead of A37/A38/A39. [REL013, REL025, REL028, REL031, REL034, REL036, REL042, REL043, REL060, REL061, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- Ordered pairs crossing the group boundaries stretched from 1–3 event positions apart to 4–5 apart (A30→A37/A38/A39 and A33/A35/A36→A31), consistent with the other three-activity group now lying between them; A33/A35/A36 also occur slightly earlier in the case (mean event position about 0.74 → 0.67) and A37/A38/A39 slightly later (about 0.73 → 0.76). [LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG011, LAG013, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- A04 largely left the main flow: it ran in about 59 in 100 cases earlier but about 26 in 100 in the later window; A14 now passes directly to A15 (about 79 in 100 of A14's observed outgoing transitions, versus about 43 earlier, when A04 took about 57), A04's own edge to A15 fell from about 90 to 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and A04, when it still runs, sits later in the case (mean event position about 0.20 → 0.38). [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- A02, A08 and A10 roughly tripled their participation (from about 6–8 to about 18–23 in 100 cases), though they remain rare and these estimates rest on only 12–50 traces per window; the successors of A45 and A47 also diversified slightly, with A46 and A48 remaining dominant (about 82–84 in 100 of their outgoing transitions). [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR009, DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the earlier behaviour — each case executing one of two alternative activity groups, {A33, A35, A36} in about half of the cases or {A37, A38, A39} in the other half, rarely both — gave way in the later window to a behaviour in which both groups execute in almost every case (about 98 in 100), one after the other (A33/A35/A36 first, then A37/A38/A39), between the always-present activities A14/A30 upstream and A31/A47/A48 downstream. The signs are direct and consistent: participation of all six activities rose from about half of cases to near-universal single execution; the cross-group relation profiles moved from mutual exclusivity to co-occurrence with a fixed order; the successor profiles of A33/A35/A36 shifted from A31 to A37/A38/A39; and boundary gaps grew from 1–3 to 4–5 event positions. Screening qualified 109 items where about 1 would be expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds those seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, so chance cannot account for the pattern as a whole. Limitations: the many relation items largely re-express one underlying change rather than confirming it independently, positions are event positions rather than clock times, and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows simply sample a different mix of case types (for example, only cases that run both groups) of an otherwise unchanged process. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, REL037, REL039, REL045, REL050, REL052, REL013, REL028, REL031, REL034, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG005, LAG013, POS005, POS008]

Other differences: A04, which earlier sat between A14 and A15, ran in only about 26 in 100 later cases (from about 59 in 100); A14 now flows directly to A15, and A04, when present, occurs later with more varied successors. A02, A08 and A10 roughly tripled their participation from low bases. A15 increasingly interleaves with the six group activities (about 41 in 100 later cases versus about 15–19 earlier). [OCC002, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
